instruction: The f1 five-pass boot-syntax suite can pass vacuously: an unguarded exit-wait on a dead child lets the process EXIT 0 even when the awaited event never resolved. Close the false-green so the suite FAILS when the child is dead.
output:
```
fix(D-3): f1 Pass 1 false-green loop-drain — guard the exit-wait on a dead child

Root cause (reproduced, root-caused, negated):
runPass1_Functional's finally did
    serverProc.kill('SIGTERM');
    await new Promise(r => serverProc.on('exit', r));
When the child already exited before this line (boot crash, port bind
failure, late SIGTERM), the 'exit' event never fires, the promise stays
pending, and nothing keeps the event loop alive — Node exits 0 and the
in-flight AssertionError is silently discarded. The harness then reports
green for a server that never booted.

Reproduction (negative test, bidirectional, harness-level):
  PAYESH_TLS_CERT/PAYESH_TLS_KEY point to missing files → child exits 1
  at module load (node --check only parses, so assertion 1.1 stays green,
  isolating the failure to the spawn phase).
  - unfixed tree (633fec46): HARNESS_EXIT=0, no FATAL  → false green
  - fixed tree:               HARNESS_EXIT=1, FATAL     → fail-fast

Minimal fix: only await an exit that can still happen.
    if (serverProc.exitCode === null && serverProc.signalCode === null) {
      await new Promise(r => serverProc.on('exit', r));
    }
This is the same guard the repo already uses in tests/delta-phase4.js
killServer(), and the same hardened-stop idiom as tests/phase2-occ-multi.js
stop() (F-A2). Pass 4 (line 183) is untouched: its child is provably alive
at kill time (assertion 4.1 just succeeded), so the trap cannot fire there.

Blast radius: one hunk, test harness only; product code untouched.
Same latent trap shape exists in tests/reaudit-occ-stale-write.js (x2) and
tests/tombstone.js (unfixed, REPORTED — no reproduction yet).

Verification:
- negative: unfixed=RED (false green) / fixed=GREEN
- positive: f1 five-pass 5/5 VERIFIED (Pass 1 boots, Pass 4 shutdown 20ms)
- boundary: Pass 4 live-server await unchanged and timed
- regression: npm test 547/547
```

```diff
     serverProc.kill('SIGTERM');
-    await new Promise(r => serverProc.on('exit', r));
+    /* D-3: اگر فرزند پیش از این خط از کار افتاده باشد (crash در بوت، شکست در
+       bind کردن پورت، یا رسیدنِ تأخیریِ SIGTERM)، رویداد 'exit' دیگر هرگز
```

```
  broken tree -> exit 1; PROBE_LEGACY=1 reproduces 10/10 false-green

Deliberately out of default suites (needs live Redis on 127.0.0.1:6379).
```


instruction: Migration 012 crashes the whole chain on hosts lacking the psql binary. Halt gracefully with a clear error instead.
Direct PG mutations (school transfer) leave a stale per-user bootstrap authorization cache; server/sync.js does not invalidate it. Add invalidation on users sync ops.
Redis cluster/sentinel retry exhaustion: the client gives up permanently after retries and never recovers. Implement bounded retry with recovery.
output:
```
fix(redis): M14-C01 — cluster/sentinel retry exhaustion (P1)

clusterRetryStrategy (times>3 => null) and sentinelRetryStrategy (times>5
=> null) surrendered permanently: ioredis treats a non-number return as
'give up' -> setStatus('end') + flushQueue, no further reconnect ever.

Impact: any cluster outage longer than ~1.8s (4 attempts) or sentinel
outage longer than ~5.25s (6 attempts) killed the client forever; only a
process restart recovered it. Sentinel's own failover takes up to 15s
(HA_REDIS.md), so the client died on every real failover — contradicting
the documented no-reboot contract. Standalone was already remediated in
Phase-2 (never null); cluster/sentinel were not.

Fix: both strategies now always return a capped backoff
(cluster <=2000ms, sentinel <=1500ms) — never null. Boot is unaffected:
connect() still rejects in ~1-2s (verified), so P0-13 fail-closed and
init() behavior are unchanged; only post-connect outage recovery improves.

Docs: HA_REDIS.md §2 corrected (was 'limited retry (5 attempts)' which
self-contradicted the no-reboot claim); BACKEND_PRODUCTION_ARCHITECTURE.md
§5 gained the never-null retry contract note.

Tests: tests/m14-c01-retry-exhaustion.js — 9/9 green (3 layers:
1000-attempt contract check, real ioredis blackhole behavior, never-'end'
assertion). C01_MUTATE=VULN restores the old null-returning strategies and
the same test suite goes green proving the assertions are load-bearing:
both clients reach 'end' (6/6 VULN assertions). freeze regenerated at
478 root docs / 644 tests; --check --freeze EXIT 0.
```

instruction: The reza-mirror-check tool passes unvalidated snapshot paths straight to fs — a path containing .. can escape the project root. Gate the paths: a whitelist of the constant snapshot paths, an identifier pattern, and an explicit error on any .. escape.

The a31 test harness builds module paths dynamically with path.join(ROOT, ...) and requires them through that string — a security-gate injection pattern. Convert every dynamic path.join require into a static relative require.
Engineering lesson — false-green-pattern: installFake (tests/cache-l2-epoch.js:25-33) was suspected as false-green; it is not — a broken fake fails E3/E5/E8.
output: A mock is only a false-green if it replaces the CODE UNDER TEST, not merely a DEPENDENCY of it. Verify by breaking the mock on purpose.

instruction: Engineering lesson — false-green-pattern: loginAs returning null does not fail the suite in tests/api/ harness paths.
output: Every helper whose null return is later dereferenced must be asserted non-null at the call site, or the suite can pass while authentication never actually happened.

instruction: Engineering lesson — ci-test-integrity-lesson: CI failure while local npm test was green.
output: Before attributing a CI failure to the change under review, check service-readiness ordering in the workflow, not just the test code.

instruction: Engineering lesson — false-green-pattern: Process EXIT 0 while awaited child event never resolved.
output: Any wait on a child must be guarded: verify the child is alive and the event actually fired before allowing exit 0.

instruction: Engineering lesson — successful-verification-approach: Route-level policy can be bypassed when a handler reaches the boundary function through an unguarded path.
output: For tenant-boundary / authorization claims: enumerate ALL call sites of the guard function plus ALL route-level policies, and check each route is actually covered.

instruction: Engineering lesson — verification-pattern: Reported defect existed at a prior HEAD; checking at current HEAD required independent confirmation.
output: Every defect verification must record the HEAD it was checked at, and any later use must re-check at the new HEAD.

instruction: Engineering lesson — scope-discipline-lesson: None — audit stayed read-only by design.
output: For audit missions: state the read-only constraint, operate on a separate worktree, and never write into the audited tree.

instruction: Engineering lesson — process-failure: Session terminated with 'You have reached the maximum number of tool-calling iterations'.
output: Long missions must be decomposed into bounded sub-missions before the cap is hit; a capped session must be marked UNCERTAIN, never SUCCESS.

instruction: Engineering lesson — self-critique-lesson: First estimate: 18 Payesh sessions. Verified count: 12.
output: Corpus membership tests must require BOTH a repo-boundary signal (path in tool output) AND an activity signal (terminal/write/patch), never a keyword alone.

instruction: Engineering lesson — self-critique-lesson: 516 raw pattern hits; 0 actual false-green commissions.
output: False-green (or any anti-pattern) scanners must classify a hit by its LOCATION: pattern inside a terminal command / write_file / patch argument = COMMISSION; pattern inside tool output = DETECTION. Only commissions count as violations.
